issues.legal_issue: The appellants’ identities as assailants were established by the evidence, so the convictions entered after reversal of their acquittals could be upheld.
material_facts: The trial court acquitted the appellants, but the High Court found that acquittal perverse and convicted them.
Several prosecution eyewitnesses identified the appellants as participants in the assault that caused the deceased’s death.
The deceased’s son promptly lodged a report naming the appellants as assailants.

The contractor, who was present at the scene, testified that the deceased was assaulted by the persons working there and identified the appellants in court; his testimony supported the prosecution account.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court found no infirmity in the High Court’s assessment that the appellants’ identities were established, upheld their convictions under Section 304 Part II read with Section 149 of the IPC and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Sections 304 Part II and 149 of the Indian Penal Code in affirming the convictions. It accepted the High Court’s assessment of the evidence, including eyewitness identification corroborated by the contractor’s testimony and the promptly lodged report, and found no reason to interfere with the High Court’s reversal of the acquittal. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.appeal_from_conviction_reversing_acquitt: The prosecution appealed an acquittal, the appellate court reversed it and convicted the accused, and the accused challenged that conviction on appeal.
predicates.multiple_eyewitnesses_identified_accused: More than one witness to the assault identified the accused as participants.
predicates.prompt_report_named_accused: A report was lodged soon after the incident and named the accused as assailants.
predicates.contractor_witness_saw_assault_and_ident: A contractor present at the scene testified that the deceased was assaulted and identified the accused in court.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a conviction entered after reversal of an acquittal, multiple eyewitnesses identify the accused, a promptly lodged report names them, and a contractor witness who saw the assault identifies them, the conviction is upheld and the appeal is dismissed.
